summary: Gogebic County, Michigan, Ottawa National Forest steel lookout built 1936; a 1977 report announced its dismantling and a cab exhibit, but completion is not confirmed.

facts.design: 110-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: A May 1977 report said the tower would be dismantled; no source we read confirms the work was done

events.note: 110-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 cab erected
May 1977 report said the tower will be dismantled; completion not confirmed

evidence.supports: location: Gogebic County, inside the Ottawa National Forest
1936 110-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 cab erected (height 33.5 m)
evidence.quote: 1936: A 110-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 cab was erected.

evidence.supports: the structure had stood over the Marenisco Township landscape since 1936
evidence.quote: Since 1936, the 110-foot steel structure has stood guard over the Marenisco Township landscape

evidence.supports: the report blamed airplanes and newer detection for the tower's end; said it would be dismantled
evidence.quote: victim of more modern types of fire detection such as use of airplanes, will be dismantled.

evidence.supports: the Forest Service hoped to keep the cab
evidence.quote: The Forest Service hopes to retain the 7 x 7 foot cab

evidence.supports: about 20 feet of steel framework to be kept
evidence.quote: approximately 20 feet of the steel framework

evidence.supports: cab and frame to go to the Sylvania Visitors Center as an exhibit on early fire detection
evidence.quote: This 'mini-tower' will be moved to the Sylvania Visitors Center to be an exhibit of early methods of fire detection.

evidence.supports: remaining steel to be offered for sale
evidence.quote: The remaining steel framework will be offered for sale.

sources.title: Matchwood
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (reprints The Wakefield News, May 19, 1977)

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Forest Lookouts page, which reprints a 1977 Wakefield News article. The 1936 date and design come from the same page. Searches for a Sylvania Visitor Center cab exhibit or for a Matchwood tower found nothing usable, so the fate is unconfirmed. The Ottawa National Forest office in Ironwood or the Wakefield News archive could confirm whether the dismantling and cab move happened. A search snippet placed Matchwood in Ontonagon County; it was not used because it came from an unverified search result.
